label: Hobbes rejected Descartes' immaterial soul, advocating strict materialism
description: Thomas Hobbes engaged in a direct critique of René Descartes's foundational principles, rejecting core axioms in favor of a dialectically opposed framework.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from René Descartes's perspective to Thomas Hobbes's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Direct contemporaneous dialogue and pedagogical transmission during the Early Modern & Scientific era.

label: Resolved Cartesian mind-body dualism by merging mind and extension into one divine substance
description: Spinoza adopted Descartes' geometric method and rationalist rigor, but exposed a fatal incoherence in Cartesian substance dualism: if substance is truly self-subsistent and infinite, there can only be one substance (Deus sive Natura), possessing infinite attributes including thought and extension.
dialecticalTension: Cartesian dualism of finite created substances (res cogitans vs. res extensa) versus Spinozist absolute monism (a single infinite substance with parallel attributes).
historicalContext: Amsterdam and The Hague, 1660s. Spinoza's first published work was an exposition of Descartes' Principles of Philosophy demonstrated geometrically (1663), before writing the Ethics.

citations.author: Baruch Spinoza
citations.quote: Except God, no substance can be or be conceived. Whatever is, is in God, and nothing can be or be conceived without God.

citations.author: René Descartes
citations.quote: By substance we can understand nothing other than a thing which exists in such a way as to depend on no other thing for its existence.

description: René Descartes formulated and introduced the concept of "Methodological Doubt & Cogito", which became a seminal contribution in epistemology philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in epistemology.
historicalContext: Introduced during the Early Modern & Scientific as part of René Descartes's canonical writings.
